forecast-period.text: A trough will approach from the west late on Saturday, move across SA on Sunday with a ridge then extending into the state from a high located southwest of WA. An upper level disturbance will move over the far west on Monday, and a cold front will slip across southern coasts later in the day and early Tuesday. The high will then move across waters to the south throughout the week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Patchy morning fog about the Lower South East district. Dry apart from an isolated shower or thunderstorm in the far southwest in the evening. Thunderstorms may be severe with damaging wind gusts and large hail possible. Maximum temperatures above average. Northwest to northeasterly winds, tending variable in the northeast at times.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms extending across the west and south throughout the day. Thunderstorms may be severe with damaging wind gusts, large hail and heavy rainfall possible in the far west during the afternoon. Maximum temperatures above average. North to northwesterly winds, shifting southwest to southeasterly from the west throughout the day.

Possible morning fog about the Agricultural Areas. Showers and isolated thunderstorms in the far west. Isolated showers developing about southern coastal districts during the afternoon, extending over the remainder of the Southern Agricultural Area in the evening. Maximum temperatures above average in the northeast, tending near average elsewhere. Southwest to southeasterly winds, freshening about the coast later.

text.p: Isolated showers and thunderstorms in the far northwest, with isolated showers possible about southern coastal districts until the afternoon. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh about the coast and northern inland areas.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: less than 2 mm about the Southern Agricultural Area, reaching up to 2 to 5 mm about southern coastal districts with local heavier falls possible between 5 to 15 mm, more likely in the South East. 5 to 15 mm is likely over areas west of about Ceduna, but local heavier falls between 20 to 40 mm are possible in the far west.
